The story goes that Graziano defeated the Etruscan army led by the powerful military commander Lars Porsenna, securing Siena's independence and laying the foundation for its later development as a city-state.

Graziano da Ratisbona, a 13th-century Dominican friar, was instrumental in the early development of the Dominican Order in Germany. He founded several monasteries and served as the first master of the Dominican province in Germany. His efforts helped establish the Dominican presence in Central Europe and contributed to the growth of the order during the Middle Ages.
